sentences.text: Shri Manish Mukharia - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/

Heard on I.A. No.3890/2024, first application filed under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal
Procedure for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

2.  This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 30.09.2023 passed in SCATR No.151/2019 by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012/ SC/ST Act, 1989) / Eleventh Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur, District Jabalpur, whereby present appellant has been convicted under Sections 366 and 376(2)(n) of IPC and sentenced to undergo ten years RI with fine of Rs.1000/- and ten years RI with fine of Rs.1000/- respectively, with default stipulation.
3. Learned counsel for the present appellant has submitted that as per the prosecution story, the prosecutrix was 16 years and 10 months old, but missing person report reveals that the father of the prosecutrix has stated that her daughter/prosecutrix was 18 years of age.

entities.text: Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012/ SC/ST Act, 1989) / Eleventh Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur, District Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The missing report in this regard available on record as Ex.28-C is also binding upon the prosecution.
As such, the age of the prosecutrix was not less than 18 years at the time of alleged incident.
It is also submitted by the counsel for appellant that entire story of the prosecution and the evidence available on record reveal that the prosecutrix was a consenting party.

She recovered after fifteen days and during this period,
she did not seek any kind of help from anyone, which could be sought for by her and this act of the 2 CRA-2149-2024 prosecutrix shows that she was a consenting party.

It is also submitted that though DNA report is positive but since it is a matter of consent and the prosecutrix was major at the time of alleged incident, therefore, the present appellant has a good case on merits.
Further, the appellant has suffered more than half of the sentence awarded to him.
It is also submitted that there is no likelihood of early hearing of the instant appeal in near future.
The appellant is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this court.
Therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant be suspended and he be released on bail.
4 . Per contra, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text:
Having considered the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, I.A.
No.3890/2024 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.

The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 09.10.2025 and on subsequent dates given by the trial Court in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE 3 CRA-2149-2024 ac/-
